passages.text: Jesus also said to His disciples, “There was a rich man whose manager was accused of wasting his possessions.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He told them a story.
There was a rich man.
This rich man had a manager.
Someone accused the manager.
They said the manager was wasting the rich man’s possessions.
passages.original: Ἔλεγεν δὲ καὶ πρὸς τοὺς μαθητάς Ἄνθρωπός τις ἦν πλούσιος ὃς εἶχεν οἰκονόμον καὶ οὗτος διεβλήθη αὐτῷ ὡς διασκορπίζων τὰ ὑπάρχοντα αὐτοῦ

passages.text: So he called him in to ask, ‘What is this I hear about you? Turn in an account of your management, for you cannot be manager any longer.’
passages.sermon:
Jesus told a story to His disciples.
A rich man had a manager.
Someone accused the manager of wasting the rich man’s possessions.
The rich man called the manager in.
He spoke to the manager.
He said, “What is this I hear about you?
Give me an account of your management.
You cannot be manager any longer.”
passages.original: καὶ φωνήσας αὐτὸν εἶπεν αὐτῷ Τί τοῦτο ἀκούω περὶ σοῦ ἀπόδος τὸν λόγον τῆς οἰκονομίας σου οὐ γὰρ δύνῃ ἔτι οἰκονομεῖν

passages.text: The manager said to himself, ‘What shall I do, now that my master is taking away my position? I am too weak to dig and too ashamed to beg.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He told them about a manager.
The manager worked for a rich man.
The rich man decided to remove the manager from his job.
The manager spoke to himself.
He said, “What will I do?”
He knew his master was taking away his position.
He said, “I am not strong enough to dig.”
He also said, “I am ashamed to beg.”
passages.original: Εἶπεν δὲ ἐν ἑαυτῷ ὁ οἰκονόμος Τί ποιήσω ὅτι ὁ κύριός μου ἀφαιρεῖται τὴν οἰκονομίαν ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ σκάπτειν οὐκ ἰσχύω ἐπαιτεῖν αἰσχύνομαι

passages.text: I know what I will do, so that after my removal from management, people will welcome me into their homes.’
passages.sermon:
The manager faced losing his job.
He thought about his situation.
He decided what to do next.
He wanted people to welcome him into their homes after he lost his position.
He made a plan to achieve this.
passages.original: ἔγνων τί ποιήσω ἵνα ὅταν μετασταθῶ ἐκ τῆς οἰκονομίας δέξωνταί με εἰς τοὺς οἴκους ἑαυτῶν

passages.text: And he called in each one of his master’s debtors. ‘How much do you owe my master?’ he asked the first.
passages.sermon:
A manager worked for a master.
The master had several debtors.
The manager called each debtor to come to him.
He spoke to the first debtor.
He asked, "How much do you owe my master?"
passages.original: Καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος ἕνα ἕκαστον τῶν χρεοφειλετῶν τοῦ κυρίου ἑαυτοῦ ἔλεγεν τῷ πρώτῳ Πόσον ὀφείλεις τῷ κυρίῳ μου

passages.text: ‘A hundred measures of olive oil,’ he answered. ‘Take your bill,’ said the manager. ‘Sit down quickly, and write fifty.’
passages.sermon:
The debtor answered the manager.
He said, "I owe a hundred measures of olive oil."
The manager spoke to him.
He said, "Take your bill."
He said, "Sit down quickly."
He said, "Write fifty."
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν Ἑκατὸν βάτους ἐλαίου Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Δέξαι σου τὰ γράμματα καὶ καθίσας ταχέως γράψον πεντήκοντα

passages.text: Then he asked another, ‘And how much do you owe?’ ‘A hundred measures of wheat,’ he replied. ‘Take your bill and write eighty,’ he told him.
passages.sermon:
The manager spoke to another debtor.
He asked, "How much do you owe?"
The debtor answered, "I owe one hundred measures of wheat."
The manager said, "Take your bill."
He told him, "Write eighty."
passages.original: Ἔπειτα ἑτέρῳ εἶπεν Σὺ δὲ πόσον ὀφείλεις Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν Ἑκατὸν κόρους σίτου Λέγει αὐτῷ Δέξαι σου τὰ γράμματα καὶ γράψον ὀγδοήκοντα

passages.text: The master commended the dishonest manager because he had acted shrewdly. For the sons of this age are more shrewd in dealing with their own kind than are the sons of light.
passages.sermon:
The master spoke about the dishonest manager.
The master saw that the manager acted shrewdly.
The master praised the manager for his shrewd actions.
People of this world are called the sons of this age.
The sons of this age act with more shrewdness toward their own people.
The sons of light are people who follow God.
The sons of this age are more shrewd than the sons of light in their own generation.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐπῄνεσεν ὁ κύριος τὸν οἰκονόμον τῆς ἀδικίας ὅτι φρονίμως ἐποίησεν ὅτι οἱ υἱοὶ τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου φρονιμώτεροι ὑπὲρ τοὺς υἱοὺς τοῦ φωτὸς εἰς τὴν γενεὰν τὴν ἑαυτῶν εἰσιν

passages.text: I tell you, use worldly wealth to make friends for yourselves, so that when it is gone, they will welcome you into eternal dwellings.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to his disciples.
Jesus gave them a command.
He said, "Use worldly wealth."
Worldly wealth means money and possessions that belong to this world.
Use this wealth to make friends for yourselves.
These friends are people you help with your wealth.
One day, your wealth will be gone.
When your wealth is gone, these friends will welcome you.
They will welcome you into eternal dwellings.
Eternal dwellings are places with God that last forever.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐγὼ ὑμῖν λέγω ἑαυτοῖς ποιήσατε φίλους ἐκ τοῦ μαμωνᾶ τῆς ἀδικίας ἵνα ὅταν ἐκλίπῃ δέξωνται ὑμᾶς εἰς τὰς αἰωνίους σκηνάς

passages.text: Whoever is faithful with very little will also be faithful with much, and whoever is dishonest with very little will also be dishonest with much.
passages.sermon:
A faithful person is trustworthy with very little.
A faithful person is also trustworthy with much.
A dishonest person is dishonest with very little.
A dishonest person is also dishonest with much.
passages.original: Ὁ πιστὸς ἐν ἐλαχίστῳ καὶ ἐν πολλῷ πιστός ἐστιν καὶ ὁ ἐν ἐλαχίστῳ ἄδικος καὶ ἐν πολλῷ ἄδικός ἐστιν

passages.text: So if you have not been faithful with worldly wealth, who will entrust you with true riches?
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to his disciples.
He taught them about faithfulness and wealth.
Worldly wealth is not true riches.
If you are not faithful with worldly wealth, you show you cannot be trusted.
If you are not faithful with money, no one will trust you with true riches.
passages.original: εἰ οὖν ἐν τῷ ἀδίκῳ μαμωνᾷ πιστοὶ οὐκ ἐγένεσθε τὸ ἀληθινὸν τίς ὑμῖν πιστεύσει

passages.text: And if you have not been faithful with the belongings of another, who will give you belongings of your own?
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to His listeners.\r\nHe taught about faithfulness.\r\nHe said, “If you are not faithful with what belongs to someone else, no one will give you your own things.”
passages.original: καὶ εἰ ἐν τῷ ἀλλοτρίῳ πιστοὶ οὐκ ἐγένεσθε τὸ ὑμέτερον τίς δώσει ὑμῖν

passages.text: No servant can serve two masters. Either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will be devoted to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve both God and money.”
passages.sermon:
A servant cannot serve two masters.
A servant must choose one master.
If a servant serves two masters, he will hate one master.
He will love the other master.
He will be loyal to one master.
He will look down on the other master.
You cannot serve God and money at the same time.
passages.original: Οὐδεὶς οἰκέτης δύναται δυσὶ κυρίοις δουλεύειν ἢ γὰρ τὸν ἕνα μισήσει καὶ τὸν ἕτερον ἀγαπήσει ἢ ἑνὸς ἀνθέξεται καὶ τοῦ ἑτέρου καταφρονήσει οὐ δύνασθε Θεῷ δουλεύειν καὶ μαμωνᾷ

passages.text: The Pharisees, who were lovers of money, heard all of this and were scoffing at Jesus.
passages.sermon: The Pharisees loved money.\r\nThey heard everything Jesus said.\r\nThey mocked Jesus.
passages.original: Ἤκουον δὲ ταῦτα πάντα οἱ Φαρισαῖοι φιλάργυροι ὑπάρχοντες καὶ ἐξεμυκτήριζον αὐτόν

passages.text: So He said to them, “You are the ones who justify yourselves before men, but God knows your hearts. For what is prized among men is detestable before God.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the Pharisees.
The Pharisees loved money.
Jesus said, "You justify yourselves in front of people.
God knows your hearts.
People value some things highly.
God finds those things detestable."
passages.original: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Ὑμεῖς ἐστε οἱ δικαιοῦντες ἑαυτοὺς ἐνώπιον τῶν ἀνθρώπων ὁ δὲ Θεὸς γινώσκει τὰς καρδίας ὑμῶν ὅτι τὸ ἐν ἀνθρώποις ὑψηλὸν βδέλυγμα ἐνώπιον τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: The Law and the Prophets were proclaimed until John. Since that time, the gospel of the kingdom of God is being preached, and everyone is forcing his way into it.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the Pharisees.
The Pharisees loved money.
Jesus said, “The Law and the Prophets were proclaimed until John.
John refers to John the Baptist.
Since John, people preach the good news of God’s kingdom.
Now, everyone tries hard to enter God’s kingdom.”
passages.original: Ὁ νόμος καὶ οἱ προφῆται μέχρι Ἰωάννου ἀπὸ τότε ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ Θεοῦ εὐαγγελίζεται καὶ πᾶς εἰς αὐτὴν βιάζεται

passages.text: But it is easier for heaven and earth to pass away than for a single stroke of a pen to drop out of the Law.
passages.sermon:
God gave the Law.
The Law is very important to God.
Heaven and earth are strong and lasting.
It is easier for heaven and earth to disappear than for one small part of the Law to fail.
Not even a single stroke of the Law will fall away.
passages.original: εὐκοπώτερον δέ ἐστιν τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν παρελθεῖν ἢ τοῦ νόμου μίαν κεραίαν πεσεῖν

passages.text: Anyone who divorces his wife and marries another woman commits adultery, and he who marries a divorced woman commits adultery.
passages.sermon: Jesus is speaking about marriage and adultery.\r\nAnyone who divorces his wife and marries another woman commits adultery.\r\nAnyone who marries a woman divorced from her husband commits adultery.
passages.original: Πᾶς ὁ ἀπολύων τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ καὶ γαμῶν ἑτέραν μοιχεύει καὶ ὁ ἀπολελυμένην ἀπὸ ἀνδρὸς γαμῶν μοιχεύει

passages.text: Now there was a rich man dressed in purple and fine linen, who lived each day in joyous splendor.
passages.sermon:
There was a man.
This man was rich.
He wore purple clothes.
He also wore fine linen.
He enjoyed himself every day.
He lived each day in great splendor.
passages.original: Ἄνθρωπος δέ τις ἦν πλούσιος καὶ ἐνεδιδύσκετο πορφύραν καὶ βύσσον εὐφραινόμενος καθ’ ἡμέραν λαμπρῶς

passages.text: And a beggar named Lazarus lay at his gate, covered with sores and longing to be fed with the crumbs that fell from the rich man’s table. Even the dogs came and licked his sores.
passages.sermon:
A poor man lay at the rich man's gate.
His name was Lazarus.
Lazarus had sores all over his body.
He wanted to eat the crumbs that fell from the rich man's table.
Dogs came to Lazarus.
The dogs licked his sores.
passages.original: πτωχὸς δέ τις ὀνόματι Λάζαρος ἐβέβλητο πρὸς τὸν πυλῶνα αὐτοῦ εἱλκωμένος καὶ ἐπιθυμῶν χορτασθῆναι ἀπὸ τῶν πιπτόντων ἀπὸ τῆς τραπέζης τοῦ πλουσίου ἀλλὰ καὶ οἱ κύνες ἐρχόμενοι ἐπέλειχον τὰ ἕλκη αὐτοῦ

passages.text: One day the beggar died and was carried by the angels to Abraham’s side. And the rich man also died and was buried.
passages.sermon:
A poor man named Lazarus lay at the rich man's gate.
Lazarus was covered with sores.
Lazarus longed to eat the crumbs from the rich man's table.
One day, Lazarus died.
Angels carried Lazarus to Abraham's side.
The rich man also died.
People buried the rich man.
passages.original: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἀποθανεῖν τὸν πτωχὸν καὶ ἀπενεχθῆναι αὐτὸν ὑπὸ τῶν ἀγγέλων εἰς τὸν κόλπον Ἀβραάμ ἀπέθανεν δὲ καὶ ὁ πλούσιος καὶ ἐτάφη

passages.text: In Hades, where he was in torment, he looked up and saw Abraham from afar, with Lazarus by his side.
passages.sermon:
The rich man died.
He went to Hades.
He suffered in torment there.
He looked up.
He saw Abraham far away.
He saw Lazarus beside Abraham.
passages.original: καὶ ἐν τῷ ᾅδῃ ἐπάρας τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτοῦ ὑπάρχων ἐν βασάνοις ὁρᾷ Ἀβραὰμ ἀπὸ μακρόθεν καὶ Λάζαρον ἐν τοῖς κόλποις αὐτοῦ

passages.text: So he cried out, ‘Father Abraham, have mercy on me and send Lazarus to dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue. For I am in agony in this fire.’
passages.sermon:
The rich man was in torment in Hades.
He looked up and saw Abraham far away.
He saw Lazarus at Abraham’s side.
The rich man cried out.
He said, “Father Abraham, have mercy on me.”
He said, “Send Lazarus to me.”
He said, “Let Lazarus dip the tip of his finger in water.”
He said, “Let him cool my tongue.”
He said, “I am in agony in this fire.”
passages.original: Καὶ αὐτὸς φωνήσας εἶπεν Πάτερ Ἀβραάμ ἐλέησόν με καὶ πέμψον Λάζαρον ἵνα βάψῃ τὸ ἄκρον τοῦ δακτύλου αὐτοῦ ὕδατος καὶ καταψύξῃ τὴν γλῶσσάν μου ὅτι ὀδυνῶμαι ἐν τῇ φλογὶ ταύτῃ

passages.text: But Abraham answered, ‘Child, remember that during your lifetime you received your good things, while Lazarus received bad things. But now he is comforted here, while you are in agony.
passages.sermon:
Abraham spoke to the rich man.
Abraham called him "Child."
Abraham told him to remember his life on earth.
Abraham said the rich man received good things during his life.
Abraham said Lazarus received bad things during his life.
Abraham said Lazarus is now comforted here.
Abraham said the rich man is now in agony.
passages.original: Εἶπεν δὲ Ἀβραάμ Τέκνον μνήσθητι ὅτι ἀπέλαβες τὰ ἀγαθά σου ἐν τῇ ζωῇ σου καὶ Λάζαρος ὁμοίως τὰ κακά νῦν δὲ ὧδε παρακαλεῖται σὺ δὲ ὀδυνᾶσαι

passages.text: And besides all this, a great chasm has been fixed between us and you, so that even those who wish cannot cross from here to you, nor can anyone cross from there to us.’
passages.sermon:
A great chasm stands between us and you.
No one can cross this chasm.
Even if someone wants to go from here to you, they cannot.
No one can cross from your side to us either.
passages.original: καὶ ἐν πᾶσι τούτοις μεταξὺ ἡμῶν καὶ ὑμῶν χάσμα μέγα ἐστήρικται ὅπως οἱ θέλοντες διαβῆναι ἔνθεν πρὸς ὑμᾶς μὴ δύνωνται μηδὲ ἐκεῖθεν πρὸς ἡμᾶς διαπερῶσιν

passages.text: ‘Then I beg you, father,’ he said, ‘send Lazarus to my father’s house, for I have five brothers. Let him warn them, so that they will not also end up in this place of torment.’
passages.sermon:
A rich man spoke to Abraham.
The rich man was suffering in torment.
He begged Abraham for help.
He said, “Father, please send Lazarus to my father’s house.
I have five brothers.
Let Lazarus warn my brothers.
Then my brothers will not come to this place of torment.”
passages.original: Εἶπεν δέ Ἐρωτῶ σε οὖν πάτερ ἵνα πέμψῃς αὐτὸν εἰς τὸν οἶκον τοῦ πατρός μου ἔχω γὰρ πέντε ἀδελφούς ὅπως διαμαρτύρηται αὐτοῖς ἵνα μὴ καὶ αὐτοὶ ἔλθωσιν εἰς τὸν τόπον τοῦτον τῆς βασάνου

passages.text: But Abraham replied, ‘They have Moses and the prophets; let your brothers listen to them.’
passages.sermon: Abraham spoke to the rich man.\r\nAbraham said, “Your brothers have Moses and the prophets.\r\nLet your brothers listen to Moses and the prophets.”
passages.original: Λέγει δὲ Ἀβραάμ Ἔχουσι Μωϋσέα καὶ τοὺς προφήτας ἀκουσάτωσαν αὐτῶν

passages.text: ‘No, father Abraham,’ he said, ‘but if someone is sent to them from the dead, they will repent.’
passages.sermon:
A man spoke to Abraham.
He said, “No, father Abraham.”
He disagreed with Abraham’s answer.
He said, “If someone goes to my brothers from the dead, they will repent.”
He believed a person returning from the dead would cause his brothers to change their ways.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν Οὐχί πάτερ Ἀβραάμ ἀλλ’ ἐάν τις ἀπὸ νεκρῶν πορευθῇ πρὸς αὐτοὺς μετανοήσουσιν

passages.text: Then Abraham said to him, ‘If they do not listen to Moses and the prophets, they will not be persuaded even if someone rises from the dead.’ ”
passages.sermon:
Abraham spoke to the man.
Abraham said, "They have Moses and the prophets."
Moses and the prophets teach God's word.
If they do not listen to Moses and the prophets, they will not believe.
Even if someone rises from the dead, they will not be persuaded."
passages.original: Εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῷ Εἰ Μωϋσέως καὶ τῶν προφητῶν οὐκ ἀκούουσιν οὐδ’ ἐάν τις ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναστῇ πεισθήσονται
